- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after spikes or high-value periods.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the middle of the horizon, then gradually rise — suggesting mean reversion bias or delayed reaction to market signals.
- After a sharp spike in true values (e.g., 50+), forecasts often overshoot and then correct downward — indicating lagged response or overreaction to recent volatility.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the horizon, particularly when true values are trending downward — suggesting horizon-specific bias toward short-term overconfidence.
- Forecasts show persistent downward bias in the last 5–7 days of the horizon, especially when true values are stabilizing or declining — implying failure to capture near-term mean reversion or trend reversal.
- Model tends to ignore recent high values in the history window, leading to underestimation of subsequent peaks — suggesting insufficient weighting of recent data or lagged sensitivity to momentum.
